slot.brief: First-order kinetics: given initial amount and amount after a time (or half-life), find the rate constant or fraction remaining

stem: A first-order reaction reduces a reactant from $100$ mg to $25$ mg in $20$ min. Find its rate constant. Take $\ln 2=0.693$.

verdicts.working: The amount decreases by a factor of 4, so 20 min is two half-lives. Thus k = ln 2 / 10 = 0.0693 min⁻¹.

working:
$k=\dfrac{1}{t}\ln\dfrac{a_0}{a_t}$
$=\dfrac{1}{20}\ln\dfrac{100}{25}$
$=\dfrac{2\ln 2}{20}=0.0693\ \text{min}^{-1}$

Independent check: The amount decreases by a factor of 4, so 20 min is two half-lives. Thus k = ln 2 / 10 = 0.0693 min⁻¹.
